threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still get confused by the bus routes. Real locals can navigate the night buses with their eyes closed and a pint in hand.
Caught the N35 last night. A guy was passionately arguing with a lamppost about his ex. No one batted an eyelid; classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you see a whole family of ducks waddling down Hermannstraße like it's their personal runway, you know you're in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab stand that doubles as an underground music venue, where you can munch while vibing with local bands.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they avoid Civic Center BART during rush hour. It’s all about that unspoken understanding of chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy juggling on the platform while waiting for the 19. Completely missed his bus, but nailed the final catch.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think all Gràcia bars close early; meanwhile, locals are just warming up at the 24-hour locales post 2 AM.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their fascination with every corner café, snapping pics like tourists while locals just grab their coffee and go.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line'. That's a surefire sign you haven't been around long.
Caught a glimpse of an old bloke serenading a pigeon on the N36 last night. Only in Peckham would that feel normal at 3 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted an artist painting a mural while a couple argued in Turkish over a spilled kebab in front of my local Späti.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find U-Bahn trains adorned with art installations, but only in Friedrichshain does it feel like walking through a gallery on your way to work.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local will turn their face away when they see a Muni bus approaching, knowing it’s just going to be another 15-minute wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni with a passenger serenading us; loud enough to drown out the usual grit, but not the smell of the street. Classic SF vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into any bar and get a proper vermut. Little do they know, the locals have their favorites and they won’t share.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still refer to the metro stops by the old names, like 'Reforma' instead of 'L3'. That and a tendency to use the bus instead of walking.
